content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm experiencing a similar problem to another user. When I tried to copy a rung in my LLD file, a Java error was displayed. After removing the rung and saving, the program wouldn't reopen and the progress bar would freeze at 100%. Trying to open the file again with [product_name] multiple times just caused the status bar to repeatedly fill to 100%. Using an older [product_name] version also didn't work. Is there any way to repair this file? Thank you for your assistance!

Hi [user_name], your issue is close to the previous user’s, but not entirely identical. The file can't be accessed due to the Java error. If your project was created with [product_name] [version_no] and hardware set to [article_no], then it cannot be opened with an older [product_name] version. The error message you receive indicates your hardware uses [article_no]. I suggest submitting a support request. Also, consider creating future programs in FBD format, as LAD seems more prone to errors.

Hello [user_name], I tried submitting a support request, but encountered an error while logging in to describe the issue. Is there another way to recover the program, since my hardware uses [article_no] (which prevents opening with older [product_name])? I need to test the application today, so any alternative solution would be appreciated. I’ll avoid using ladder format in [product_name] going forward. Thank you!

The file you uploaded has the '.lld' extension, indicating it is a LAD file. I'm not aware of any method to open this file. The error during your support request may be due to a server problem from [company_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter file corruption and software freezing when working with '.lld' (LAD) files in [product_name], especially after Java errors during edits or saves. After running into the error, the software repeatedly fails to load corrupted files, looping the progress bar. Attempts to use older versions of the software fail because of hardware incompatibility. Several users highlight concerns about the LAD editor's reliability and the challenges involved in recovering damaged project files.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the software to reliably manage edits and saves without corrupting files, offer backward compatibility or efficient file recovery options, and provide accessible support channels during critical issues.
